sections.title: InspectAI Studio 4 - User Guide
sections.summary: InspectAI Studio builds visual inspection models for production lines: it classifies parts, finds anomalies and reads printed text.
sections.text: InspectAI Studio builds visual inspection models for production lines: it classifies parts, finds anomalies and reads printed text.

sections.title: 1.1 System Requirements
sections.summary: A workstation with Windows 11, 32 GB of memory and an NVIDIA GPU with at least 8 GB of video memory.
sections.text: A workstation with Windows 11, 32 GB of memory and an NVIDIA GPU with at least 8 GB of video memory. Training on the CPU is possible but about twenty times slower.

sections.title: 1.2 Installation
sections.summary: Run InspectAI_Studio_4_Setup.exe as an administrator and accept the licence.
sections.text: Run InspectAI_Studio_4_Setup.exe as an administrator and accept the licence. The installer adds the CUDA runtime it needs; no separate driver package is required.

sections.title: 1.3 Activating the Licence
sections.summary: Open Help > Licence, paste the 25 character licence key and click Activate.
sections.text: Open Help > Licence, paste the 25-character licence key and click Activate. An offline workstation shows a request code instead; send it to support and paste the reply file.

sections.title: 2 Image Classification
sections.summary: Image Classification sorts each image of a part into one of the classes you define, for example OK, Scratch and Dent.
sections.text: Image Classification sorts each image of a part into one of the classes you define, for example OK, Scratch and Dent.

sections.title: 2.1 Project Setup
sections.summary: Click New Project, choose Image Classification, name the project and pick the folder where it is stored.
sections.text: Click New Project, choose Image Classification, name the project and pick the folder where it is stored. Add the class names in the Classes panel; at least two classes are needed.

sections.title: 2.2 Importing Images
sections.summary: Images can come from a folder on disk or straight from a line camera.
sections.text: Images can come from a folder on disk or straight from a line camera. 2.2.1 Option A: From a folder Click Import > Folder and select a parent folder with one subfolder per class; each subfolder name must match a class name. Images in other subfolders are skipped. 2.2.2 Option B: From a camera Click Import > Camera, select the GigE camera in the list and press Capture for each part. Assign the class with the number keys 1 to 9 while capturing.

sections.title: 2.3 Labelling
sections.summary: Open the Gallery, select the images of one class and press L to label them.
sections.text: Open the Gallery, select the images of one class and press L to label them. Unlabelled images are shown with a grey border and are left out of training.

sections.title: 2.4 Training
sections.summary: Click Train, keep the default backbone ResNet 34 and set Epochs to 40.
sections.text: Click Train, keep the default backbone ResNet-34 and set Epochs to 40. Training stops early when the validation accuracy has not improved for 8 epochs.

sections.title: 2.5 Validation
sections.summary: Open the Validation tab after training: the confusion matrix shows which classes are mixed up.
sections.text: Open the Validation tab after training: the confusion matrix shows which classes are mixed up. Aim for at least 98 percent accuracy on the hold-out images before deployment.

sections.title: 2.6 Deployment
sections.summary: Click Export and choose ONNX for the line PC or TensorRT for the edge box.
sections.text: Click Export and choose ONNX for the line PC or TensorRT for the edge box. The exported model keeps the class names and the input size of 224 x 224 pixels.

sections.title: 3 Anomaly Detection
sections.summary: Anomaly Detection learns from good parts only and marks anything that differs from them, without classes.
sections.text: Anomaly Detection learns from good parts only and marks anything that differs from them, without classes.

sections.title: 3.1 Project Setup
sections.summary: Click New Project and choose Anomaly Detection.
sections.text: Click New Project and choose Anomaly Detection. Only good parts are needed for training; keep a few defective parts aside for validation.

sections.title: 3.2 Importing Images
sections.summary: Good part images can come from a folder or from the line camera.
sections.text: Good-part images can come from a folder or from the line camera. 3.2.1 Option A: From a folder Click Import > Folder and select a folder with good parts only. At least 200 images are recommended. 3.2.2 Option B: From a camera Click Import > Camera and capture good parts during a normal production run; the capture pauses automatically when the line stops.

sections.title: 3.3 Training
sections.summary: Click Train and set the Patch Size to 32.
sections.text: Click Train and set the Patch Size to 32. Anomaly training takes about ten minutes for 500 images on an 8 GB GPU.

sections.title: 3.4 Validation
sections.summary: Load the defective parts kept aside and adjust the Threshold slider until every defective part is flagged.
sections.text: Load the defective parts kept aside and adjust the Threshold slider until every defective part is flagged. A threshold between 0.4 and 0.6 suits most parts.

sections.title: 3.5 Deployment
sections.summary: Click Export and choose ONNX.
sections.text: Click Export and choose ONNX. The threshold set during validation is stored in the exported model.

sections.title: 4 Text Reading (OCR)
sections.summary: Text Reading reads printed or engraved characters such as batch codes and serial numbers.
sections.text: Text Reading reads printed or engraved characters such as batch codes and serial numbers.

sections.title: 4.1 Project Setup
sections.summary: Click New Project, choose Text Reading and enter the character set, for example A Z and 0 9.
sections.text: Click New Project, choose Text Reading and enter the character set, for example A-Z and 0-9.

sections.title: 4.2 Annotating Text
sections.summary: Characters can be annotated by hand or proposed by the built in reader and then corrected.
sections.text: Characters can be annotated by hand or proposed by the built-in reader and then corrected. 4.2.1 Method 1: Manual annotation Draw a box around each line of text and type its characters. This suits fonts the built-in reader does not know. 4.2.2 Method 2: Assisted annotation Click Propose: the built-in reader fills in each line and you correct the mistakes. This is about three times faster for standard fonts.

sections.title: 4.3 Training
sections.summary: Click Train and set Epochs to 60.
sections.text: Click Train and set Epochs to 60. A text model needs about 300 annotated lines to read reliably.

sections.title: 4.4 Validation
sections.summary: The Validation tab shows the character error rate; aim for less than 1 percent before deployment.
sections.text: The Validation tab shows the character error rate; aim for less than 1 percent before deployment.

sections.title: 5.1 Epochs
sections.summary: The number of passes over the training images.
sections.text: The number of passes over the training images. More epochs can help small data sets but take longer.

sections.title: 5.2 Learning Rate
sections.summary: How large each training step is.
sections.text: How large each training step is. The default of 0.001 suits almost every project.

sections.title: 5.3 GPU Selection
sections.summary: Choose the GPU in Settings > Hardware when the workstation has more than one.
sections.text: Choose the GPU in Settings > Hardware when the workstation has more than one.
